accepted.question_text: For integers k > 1 and D > 3, let chi_k(D) be the maximum chromatic number of G^k over all graphs G with maximum degree at most D, and let omega_k(D) be the corresponding maximum clique number of G^k. Is it always true that chi_k(D) = omega_k(D) for every such pair (k, D)?

evidence.quote: Wegner’s Conjecture ([183]). For all integers k > 1 and D > 3, let χ_k(D) and ω_k(D) denote, respectively, the maximums over all graphs G with ∆ 6 D of χ(Gk) and ω(Gk). For all k and D we have χ_k(D) = ω_k(D).

For all integers k > 1 and D > 3, let χ_k(D) and ω_k(D) denote, respectively, the maximums over all graphs G with ∆ 6 D of χ(Gk) and ω(Gk). For all k and D we have χ_k(D) = ω_k(D). This is called Wegner’s Conjecture. It is trivially true for k = 1. For k = 2, it is proved for D ∈ {2, 3, 4, 5, 7}.

accepted.question_text: For each integer t, does there exist a threshold Delta_t such that every graph G with maximum degree Delta(G) > Delta_t satisfies omega(G^2) <= Delta(G)^2 - t? If such a threshold exists, can the same conclusion be strengthened from the clique number of G^2 to the coloring, list-coloring, painting, or Alon-Tarsi parameters of G^2, namely chi(G^2), chi_l(G^2), chi_p(G^2), or chi_AT(G^2)?
accepted.context_brief: Defect below Delta squared in graph squares

evidence.quote: Question 4. For each integer t, does there exist a constant ∆t such that all graphs G with ∆ > ∆t satisfy ω^2(G) 6 ∆2 − t? Can this conclusion be strengthened further to (i) χ2(G) 6 ∆2 − t, (ii) χ2_ℓ(G) 6 ∆2 − t, (iii) χ2_p(G) 6 ∆2 − t, or even (iv) χ2_AT(G) 6 ∆2 − t?

For each integer t, there exists a constant ∆t such that all G with ∆ > ∆t satisfy ω^2(G) 6 ∆2 − t. This conclusion can be strengthened further to (i) χ2(G) 6 ∆2 − t, (ii) χ2_ℓ(G) 6 ∆2 − t, (iii) χ2_p(G) 6 ∆2 − t, and even (iv) χ2_AT(G) 6 ∆2 − t. This is Question 4.

accepted.question_text: If G is a planar graph of maximum degree Delta(G), must the chromatic number of its square satisfy chi(G^2) <= floor(3 Delta(G) / 2) + 1 whenever Delta(G) > 8, together with the sharp small-degree cases stated by Wegner's planar graph conjecture?

evidence.quote: Wegner’s Planar Graph Conjecture ([183]). If G is planar with maximum degree ∆, then χ2(G) 6 7 if ∆ = 3, ∆ + 5 if 4 6 ∆ 6 7, and floor(3∆/2) + 1 if ∆ > 8.

Every planar graph G with maximum degree ∆(G) > 8 satisfies χ2(G) 6 floor(3∆/2) + 1. This is Wegner’s Planar Graph Conjecture (which also conjecture sharp bounds on χ2(G) for planar graphs with smaller maximum degree). This conjecture is known to hold asymptotically, even for list coloring (see Theorem 6): For each ǫ > 0 there exists ∆ǫ such that if G is a planar graph with ∆ > ∆ǫ, then χ2_ℓ(G) 6 3∆(1 + ǫ)/2.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a minor-closed class of graphs that excludes K_{3,t} for some positive integer t. Does there exist a threshold Delta_0 such that every graph G in this class with Delta(G) > Delta_0 satisfies both chi(G^2) <= chi_l(G^2) and chi_l(G^2) <= floor(3 Delta(G) / 2) + 1?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 9 ([91]). If G is a nice class of graphs, then there exists ∆0 such that if G ∈ G and ∆(G) > ∆0, then χ2(G) 6 χ2_ℓ(G) 6 floor(3∆(G)/2) + 1.

If G is a minor-closed class of graphs that excludes K3,t for some integer t, then there exists ∆0 such that if G ∈ G and ∆(G) > ∆0, then χ2(G) 6 χ2_ℓ(G) 6 floor(3∆(G)/2) + 1. This is Conjecture 9, due to Havet, van den Heuvel, McDiarmid, and Reed.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an integer D such that every 2-degenerate graph G with Delta(G) > D satisfies chi(G^2) <= 5 Delta(G) / 2? More generally, does there exist an integer D such that every graph G with Delta(G) > D and maximum average degree mad(G) < 4 also satisfies chi(G^2) <= 5 Delta(G) / 2?

evidence.quote: Question 24 ([96]). Is there an integer D such that every graph G with ∆(G) > D that is 2-degenerate satisfies χ2(G) 6 5∆(G)/2?
Question 25 ([96]). Is there an integer D such that every graph G with ∆(G) > D and mad(G) < 4 satisfies χ2(G) 6 5∆(G)/2?

There exists an integer D such that every graph G with ∆(G) > D that is 2-degenerate satisfies χ2(G) 6 5∆(G)/2. More generally, there exists an integer D such that every graph G with ∆(G) > D and mad(G) < 4 satisfies χ2(G) 6 5∆(G)/2. These are Questions 24 and 25. They are both best possible due to the construction in Theorem 23.

accepted.question_text: If G is a graph of maximum degree Delta, must its strong edge-chromatic number satisfy chi_s(G) <= 5 Delta^2 / 4 when Delta is even and chi_s(G) <= (5 Delta^2 - 2 Delta + 1) / 4 when Delta is odd? Equivalently, is the Erdos-Nesetril conjecture on strong edge coloring always true?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 26. If G is a graph with maximum degree ∆, then χ_s(G) 6 5∆2/4 if ∆ is even, and (5∆2−2∆+1)/4 if ∆ is odd.
Every graph G with maximum degree ∆ satisfies χ_s(G) 6 1.25∆2. This is the Erd˝os–Neˇsetˇril Conjecture. The best bound for general ∆ is χ_s(G) 6 1.772∆2; see the end of Section 4.1.

accepted.question_text: If a bipartite graph G has bipartition (A, B), maximum degree Delta_A on side A, and maximum degree Delta_B on side B, must its strong edge-chromatic number satisfy chi_s(G) <= Delta_A Delta_B?
accepted.context_brief: Strong edge coloring of bipartite graphs

evidence.quote: Conjecture 27 ([41]). If G is bipartite with parts A and B, then χ_s(G) 6 ∆A∆B, where ∆A and ∆B are the maximum degrees, respectively, of vertices in A and B.
If G is bipartite with parts A and B and maximum degrees (in these parts) ∆A and ∆B, then χ_s(G) 6 ∆A∆B. This is Conjecture 27, due to Brualdi and Quinn.

accepted.question_text: If a graph G has maximum degree Delta and contains no cycle of length 5, must its strong edge-chromatic number satisfy chi_s(G) <= Delta^2?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 28 ([144]). If G is a graph with no 5-cycle, then χ_s(G) 6 ∆2.
If G has maximum degree ∆ and has no 5-cycle, then χ_s(G) 6 ∆2. This is Conjecture 28, due to Mahdian.

accepted.question_text: If G is a subcubic bipartite graph with no 4-cycle, must its strong edge-chromatic number satisfy chi_s(G) <= 7?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 31 ([81]). If G is a graph with ∆ = 3, then the following six bounds hold. ... (e) χ_s(G) 6 7 if G is bipartite with no 4-cycle.
If G is subcubic and bipartite and G has no 4-cycle, then χ_s(G) 6 7. This is Conjecture 31(e), due to Faudree, Schelp, Gy´arf´as, and Tuza.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a bridgeless subcubic graph. If G is neither the Wagner graph nor the graph obtained from K_{3,3} by subdividing one edge, must chi_s(G) <= 9 hold?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 32. Let G be a subcubic graph. (a) [97] If G is bridgeless and is neither the Wagner graph nor the graph formed from the complete bipartite graph K3,3 by subdividing one edge, then χ_s(G) 6 9.

Let G be a subcubic bridgeless graph. If G is neither the Wagner graph nor the graph formed from K3,3 by subdiving an edge, then χ_s(G) 6 9. This is Conjecture 32(a), due to Hocquard, Lajou, and Luˇzar.

accepted.question_text: For subcubic graphs, do the following stronger strong-edge-coloring bounds hold: first, if G is bridgeless and has more than 13 vertices, then chi_s(G) <= 8; second, if G has girth at least 5, then chi_s(G) <= 7?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 32. Let G be a subcubic graph. ... (b) [141] If G is bridgeless and |V (G)| > 13, then χ_s(G) 6 8. (c) [141] If G has girth at least 5, then χ_s(G) 6 7.

Let G be a subcubic graph. If G is bridgeless and |V (G)| > 13, then χ_s(G) 6 8. If G has girth at least 5, then χ_s(G) 6 7. These are Conjecture 32(b,c), due to Luˇzar, Maˇcajov´a, Skoviera, and Sot´ak.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a constant C such that every planar graph G of girth g > 5 and maximum degree Delta satisfies chi_s(G) <= ceil(2 g (Delta - 1) / (g - 1)) + C?
accepted.context_brief: Planar strong edge coloring with girth

evidence.quote: Conjecture 36 ([105]). There exists a constant C such that if G is any planar graph with girth g > 5 and maximum degree ∆, then χ_s(G) 6 ceil(2g(∆ − 1)/(g − 1)) + C.

There exists a constant C such that if G is any planar graph with girth g > 5 and maximum degree ∆, then χ_s(G) 6 ceil(2g(∆−1)/(g−1)) + C. This is Conjecture 36, due to Hud´ak, Luˇzar, Sot´ak, and Skrekovski.

accepted.question_text: Does every graph G satisfy the total-coloring bound chi''(G) <= Delta(G) + 2?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 37 ([12, 171, 172]). Every graph G satisfies χ′′(G) 6 ∆ + 2.

Every graph G satisfies χ′′(G) 6 ∆ + 2. This is Conjecture 37, posed independently by Bezhad and by Vizing. Asymptotically, the best result on this problem is that there exists a constant C such that χ′′(G) 6 ∆ + C; see Theorem 38.

accepted.question_text: If a graph G has maximum degree Delta, must its L(2,1)-labeling number satisfy lambda_{2,1}(G) <= Delta^2?

evidence.quote: L(2, 1)-Labeling Conjecture ([86]). Every graph G has λ2,1(G) 6 ∆2.
If graph G has maximum degree ∆, then λ2,1(G) 6 ∆2. This is the L(2, 1)-Labeling Conjecture, due to Griggs and Yeh. It has been proved for ∆ sufficiently large; see Theorem 41.

accepted.question_text: Fix integers k > 3 and Delta > 3. For all but finitely many connected graphs G of maximum degree Delta, is the list-chromatic number of the k-th power bounded by chi_l(G^k) <= sum_{i=1}^k Delta (Delta - 1)^(i-1) + 1 - k, and does the same bound also hold for the painting number chi_p(G^k)?
accepted.context_brief: Higher graph powers list coloring and painting

evidence.quote: Bonamy and Bousquet [16] showed, for each k > 3 and graph G with maximum degree ∆, that χ_k_ℓ(G) 6 Dk,∆ − 1. And they conjectured something even stronger: For each integer k > 3, except for a finite number of graphs G, every connected graph G satisfies χ_k_ℓ(G) 6 Dk,∆ + 1 − k.
The reasoning above suggests that perhaps also χ_k_p(G) 6 Dk,∆ +1−k, but we are unaware of any progress in this direction.

Fix integers k > 3 and ∆ > 3. For all but finitely many connected graphs G with maximum degree ∆, we have χ_k_ℓ(G) 6 sum_{i=1}^k ∆(∆ − 1)i−1 + 1 − k. The same bound holds for χ_k_p(G). This would be a list coloring, or painting, analogue of Theorem 43. (In fact, both assertions were only posed as questions.)
